questions.q: Who were the four sons of Issachar?
questions.a: Issachar’s four sons were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.

questions.q: What kind of men were the sons of Tola?
questions.a: They were strong, courageous men.

questions.q: What was the number of warriors listed for these clans of Issachar?
questions.a: There were 36,000 warriors because their families had grown large through many wives and children.

questions.q: What was the number of fighting men from the tribe of Issachar?
questions.a: The tribe of Issachar had 87,000 fighting men.

questions.q: For what were the sons of Bela known?
questions.a: The sons of Bela were known as soldiers and leaders of clans.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Becher, and how many warriors were counted in his clan?
questions.a: Becher’s sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth, and his clan had 20,200 warriors.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Bilhan, and how many warriors were in that clan?
questions.a: Bilhan’s sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar, and the clan had 17,200 warriors ready for battle.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Naphtali, and who was their mother?
questions.a: Naphtali’s sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, and their mother was Bilhah.

questions.q: Who bore Manasseh a male child named Asriel?
questions.a: Manasseh’s Aramean concubine bore him a male child named Asriel.

questions.q: What was different about Zelophehad’s children?
questions.a: Zelophehad had only daughters, no sons.

questions.q: What name did Maacah give her son?
questions.a: She named him Peresh.

questions.q: Who was the son of Ulam?
questions.a: Bedan was Ulam’s son.

questions.q: Who were the descendants of Ephraim, from Shuthelah down to the second Tahath?
questions.a: Shuthelah’s son was Bered, Bered’s son was Tahath, Tahath’s son was Eleadah, and Eleadah’s son was also named Tahath.

questions.q: Why did Ephraim need comfort from his brothers when he was in mourning for many days?
questions.a: Ephraim needed comfort from his brothers because his sons Ezer and Elead were killed by men of Gath when they went to steal their cattle.

questions.q: Why did Ephraim name his son Beriah?
questions.a: Ephraim named his son Beriah because tragedy had come to his family.

questions.q: What did Ephraim’s daughter Sheerah build?
questions.a: She built Lower and Upper Beth Horon, and Uzzen Sheerah.

questions.q: Who was the son of Non?
questions.a: Joshua was the son of Non.

questions.q: Where were the possessions and residences of the descendants of Ephraim?
questions.a: Their possessions and residences included Bethel and its surrounding villages, Naaran to the east, and Gezer and Shechem to the west, as far as Ayyah.

questions.q: What cities did the descendants of Joseph control near the territory of Manasseh?
questions.a: They controlled Beth Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, Dor, and their surrounding villages.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Asher, and who were the sons of Beriah?
questions.a: Asher’s sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, with a sister named Serah. Beriah’s sons were Heber and Malchiel.

questions.q: What were the qualities of the descendants of Asher?
questions.a: The descendants of Asher were originators of clans, leaders of their families, distinguished men, fighting men, and chief among the leaders.

commentary.text: —Here is no account either of Zebulun or Dan. We can assign no reason why they only should be omitted; but it is the disgrace of the tribe of Dan, that idolatry began in that colony which fixed in Laish, and called it Dan, Jud 18 and there one of the golden calves was set up by Jeroboam. Dan is omitted, Re 7. Men become abominable when they forsake the worship of the true God, for any creature object.
